teaser.text: JPMorgan Chase sells financial access: it takes deposits, makes loans, moves payments, manages investments, and helps institutions raise and trade money. A dollar can enter as a customer’s deposit or payment, become funding or a service fee, and leave through loans, wages, technology, losses, and taxes.

stock.meta_description: JPMorgan Chase stock forecast: weighted scenarios, earnings drivers, shareholder cash returns, and today's valuation.
stock.opening: On October 14, 2026, the weighted case is $351.06 in October 2027 and $429.58 in October 2029. It hinges on durable earnings and capital generation.
stock.closing: The full JPMorgan Chase memo also examines JPMorgan Chase's business, its rivals, its management and its risks.

blocks.heading: Where could JPMorgan Chase's shares be by 2029?

paragraphs.text: The forecast’s central outcome is moderate appreciation, with meaningful downside and considerable upside around it. The probability-weighted price is $351.06 in October 2027, representing an 8% total return with dividends. It rises to $388.12 in October 2028, or 21%, and $429.58 in October 2029, or 36%.

By October 2029, the bear-to-bull range is $280.32 to $589.60, versus today’s $331.43. The bear receives 25% probability, the base 55%, and the bull 20% because durable earnings and capital generation are more likely than either severe deterioration or sustained premium expansion.

blocks.heading: What has to go right for JPMorgan Chase, and what could go wrong?

paragraphs.text: Deposit pricing, card balances, provisions and expenses decide whether the 2027 income case becomes lasting earnings. The January 14, 2027 earnings call should sharpen expense guidance. The November 2026 interchange settlement hearing and anticipated Investor Day in the first quarter of 2027 are further checkpoints. Higher charge-offs or faster expense growth weaken the case; stable credit and productive investment spending strengthen it.

blocks.heading: How much cash does JPMorgan Chase really make and give back?

paragraphs.text: Profit is not automatically distributable cash. JPMorgan recognized about $3.6 billion of noncash share-based compensation in 2025, and awards settled with shares can offset repurchases. Capital, liquidity and the share count therefore need to be read together.

blocks.heading: What does an investor pay for JPMorgan Chase today?

paragraphs.text: At $331.43 on October 14, 2026, JPMorgan’s market value was $880,146 million. The trailing P/E, or price-to-earnings ratio, tells how much investors pay for each dollar of recent earnings. JPMorgan’s trailing P/E was 13.9x, while its forward P/E was 13.3x. Those multiples imply roughly $23.84 and $24.92 of earnings per share. The modest difference says investors expect some improvement, but not an explosive leap.

dividend.title: JPMorgan Chase dividend
dividend.meta_description: JPMorgan Chase pays a quarterly dividend, shows where cash goes, and outlines the risks and yield investors should watch.
dividend.opening: JPMorgan Chase pays a $1.65 quarterly dividend, or $6.60 annualized. Its profits support the dividend, but capital and liquidity mean not all profit is distributable cash.
dividend.closing: The full memo also answers how JPMorgan Chase earns, compares with rivals, is run by management, and faces risks.

blocks.heading: How much does JPMorgan Chase pay in dividends?

paragraphs.text: JPMorgan’s current policy is more cautious about distributions. Although the board renewed a $50 billion buyback authorization, September-quarter net repurchases were only $664 million, alongside a $1.65 quarterly dividend. An authorization permits purchases; it does not require them. Jamie Dimon said management saw attractive opportunities to redeploy capital internally, which makes the next test whether new lending and investment can earn more than returning that capital.

blocks.heading: What could change JPMorgan Chase's dividend?

paragraphs.text: Dividends start from the current $6.60 annualized rate. The base reaches $7.05 in the first window and $7.20 in the second, then $7.80 in the third. The bear freezes at $6.60, while the bull rises from $7.20 to $8.80. The base follows JPMorgan’s record of annual increases and its roughly quarter-of-earnings payout, but the bear allows capital preservation to delay increases.

The forecast would move toward the bear case in 2027–2029 if deposit repricing outpaced asset yields, weakening net interest income and margins. In 2028–2029, higher charge-offs or provisions would reduce earnings and buyback capacity; expense growth that outran revenue would also compress the multiple.

blocks.heading: What is JPMorgan Chase's dividend yield today?

paragraphs.text: The shares trade at 2.5x book value and 2.9x tangible book value. They offer a 2.0% dividend yield and 3.6% buyback yield. Buybacks reduced diluted share count by 3.4% in 2025.

earnings.title: JPMorgan Chase earnings: date and guidance
earnings.meta_description: JPMorgan Chase reports next on January 14, 2027; its outlook points to income growth, while the release will sharpen expense guidance.
earnings.opening: JPMorgan Chase's next results are expected on January 14, 2027. Watch whether rising expenses support higher business volumes or consume earning power.
earnings.closing: The full memo also explains JPMorgan Chase's business, its rivals, its management and its risks.

blocks.heading: What has JPMorgan Chase guided for 2026?

paragraphs.text: For 2026, JPMorgan expects net interest income excluding Markets of $97,200 million and total net interest income of $106,200 million. The fourth-quarter outlook is $25,500 million excluding Markets and $28,000 million in total. Adjusted expenses are expected to reach $108,600 million for the year, including $27,500 million in the fourth quarter. The card net charge-off forecast is 3.2%, meaning the annualized share of card loans expected to be written off after recoveries.

The preliminary 2027 central case is $107,000 million of net interest income excluding Markets. Annualizing the fourth-quarter pace gives $102,000 million, so the case assumes further growth. About a quarter of the expected benefit comes from rate increases already reflected in the forward curve; the rest depends mainly on deposits, card loans and mix. The budget is unfinished, so expenses could absorb some of that gain.

blocks.heading: Has JPMorgan Chase kept its past promises?

paragraphs.text: JPMorgan has completed at least one such commitment. Its compensation committee certified that Dimon’s January 2023 award earned the maximum amount for the three-year period ending in December 2025. The delivered shares then remained subject to a two-year holding period.

blocks.heading: What are JPMorgan Chase's revenue and profit trends?

paragraphs.text: Revenue reached $50,172 million in September 2026. Net income was $15,305 million and diluted EPS was $5.57. Net interest income rose 12.8%, while NIM stayed at 2.5%, so the bank earned more interest dollars without widening its aggregate spread.

blocks.heading: What should investors watch in JPMorgan Chase's next release?

paragraphs.text: The scheduled January 14, 2027 earnings call should provide firmer expense guidance. Investors will need to separate spending that supports higher business volumes from investment that carries forward and costs driven by inflation. That distinction will show whether rising expenses accompany more earning power or consume it.
